This note describes how `src/tomli/_parser.py` parses TOML multiline basic
strings (`"""..."""`), with particular attention to line-ending backslashes.

## Entry point and dispatch

`parse_value` inspects the first character. When it sees `"` it checks
`src.startswith('"""', pos)`; if so it calls
`parse_multiline_str(src, pos, literal=False)`. (A single `"` goes to
`parse_one_line_basic_str` instead.)

## `parse_multiline_str`

`parse_multiline_str` handles both basic (`"""`) and literal (`'''`) multiline
strings; the `literal` flag selects the branch.

1. It advances `pos += 3` past the opening delimiter.
2. If the very next character is a newline, it is skipped (`pos += 1`). This
   implements the TOML rule that a newline immediately following the opening
   delimiter is trimmed.
3. For the basic-string case it delegates the body to
   `parse_basic_str(src, pos, multiline=True)`.
4. After the body, it allows the closing delimiter to be 4 or 5 quotes long:
   up to two extra `"` characters are appended to the result. This is what
   makes `""""` and `"""""` parse as a string ending in one or two quotes.

## `parse_basic_str` (multiline mode)

`parse_basic_str` is the core scanner. With `multiline=True` it:

- uses `ILLEGAL_MULTILINE_BASIC_STR_CHARS` as the set of forbidden control
  characters (control chars except tab and newline), so raw newlines are
  allowed inside the string;
- selects `parse_basic_str_escape_multiline` as the escape handler.

It walks the source character by character, accumulating literal runs in
`result` and flushing them whenever it hits a `"` or `\`:

- On `"`: if the next three characters are `"""`, the string ends and the
  parser returns `pos + 3`. Otherwise the quote is an ordinary character and
  scanning continues (this is how one or two quotes may appear inside a
  multiline string).
- On `\`: the pending literal run is flushed, the escape handler is invoked,
  and its returned text is appended.
- On any character in `error_on`: a `TOMLDecodeError` is raised.
- End of input before a closing delimiter raises `"Unterminated string"`.

## Escapes and line-ending backslashes

`parse_basic_str_escape_multiline` is a thin wrapper that calls
`parse_basic_str_escape(src, pos, multiline=True)`.

`parse_basic_str_escape` first reads the two-character `escape_id`. In
multiline mode, if `escape_id` is one of `"\\ "`, `"\\\t"` or `"\\\n"` (a
backslash followed by a space, tab, or newline), it treats the backslash as a
**line-ending backslash**:

- If the escape is not already `"\\\n"`, it skips spaces/tabs
  (`skip_chars(src, pos, TOML_WS)`) and requires the next character to be a
  newline; anything else raises `"Unescaped '\\' in a string"`. This enforces
  that trailing whitespace after the backslash is only allowed up to the end
  of the line.
- It then skips all following whitespace *and* newlines
  (`skip_chars(src, pos, TOML_WS_AND_NEWLINE)`), consuming the newline and any
  leading whitespace on subsequent lines.
- It returns an empty replacement string, so the backslash, the newline, and
  the following indentation are all removed from the parsed value.

For all other escapes the function falls through to the normal handling:
`\x`/`\u`/`\U` go to `parse_hex_char` (which validates hex digits and Unicode
scalar values), and the remaining two-character escapes are looked up in
`BASIC_STR_ESCAPE_REPLACEMENTS`. An unknown escape raises
`"Unescaped '\\' in a string"`.

## Related helpers

- `skip_chars` — advances `pos` while characters belong to a given set; used
  for whitespace/newline skipping.
- `skip_until` — used by the literal (`'''`) branch to find the closing
  delimiter while rejecting illegal characters.
- `parse_hex_char` — decodes `\x`, `\u`, `\U` escapes.
- `ILLEGAL_MULTILINE_BASIC_STR_CHARS`, `TOML_WS`, `TOML_WS_AND_NEWLINE`,
  `BASIC_STR_ESCAPE_REPLACEMENTS` — module-level constants driving the above.

       -> parse_basic_str(multiline=True)
